chosen.title: The Orifice and Foundation
chosen.idea: An architectural cross-section schematic modeling capital flow mechanics. At the top, a massive solid reservoir representing the $159M lending market drains through a narrow, measured throttle representing the $1.2M AMM pool. Underneath, instead of a buckling pipe, sits an immense unyielding bedrock slab labeled 'Stellar Settlement Layer: 0.1 Utilization / 100 Base Fee' absorbing the liquidations without deflection or network backpressure.
chosen.why: Translates abstract DeFi liquidity mechanics into tangible mechanical engineering terms, making the distinction between pool slippage and network capacity instantly legible.

all.title: The 128:1 Asymmetry
all.idea: Monolithic typographic stat '128:1' rendered in sharp matte white on a dark slate surface, with micro-annotations detailing the exact figures: $159,033,033 Blend TVL over $1,239,028 Soroswap TVL. Across the base runs a minimal telemetry strip confirming Stellar ledger capacity at 0.1 and base fee at 100 stroops, anchoring the mathematical reality that market depth is outpaced while network headroom remains virtually untouched.
all.why: Leads directly with the overwhelming mathematical disparity between debt and exchange liquidity, turning raw scale into an immediate visceral tension.

all.title: Decoupled Fault Lines
all.idea: A stark horizontal split composition contrasting two operational realities. The top section, rendered in dense warning tones, diagrams the pool-level bottleneck where $159M in credit risk crowds into a $1.2M AMM liquidity conduit. The bottom section, rendered in calm structural gray, shows the base ledger telemetry: flatline 0.1 capacity utilization and 100 stroop fee baseline. A rigid structural barrier between the two proves that market slippage cannot compromise transaction settlement.
all.why: This is the strongest concept because the core thesis is isolation of risk. By visually partitioning AMM depth slippage from ledger stability across a distinct horizontal boundary, it immediately communicates that pool-level liquidation friction cannot cascade into consensus gridlock.
